event.title: Wholesale customers cut spring orders; inventory ages

sources.text: Synthetic scenario document for the Crocs hypothetical private-credit scenario. Sales note dated February 19, 2027. Two wholesale customers reduced confirmed spring 2027 orders by a combined $22.0 million in the fiscal quarter ending March 31, 2027, citing slower sell-through of late-arriving winter product. The chief financial officer first learned of the reductions on February 17, 2027 and the Borrower delivered written notice to the Lender on February 19, 2027. Direct-to-consumer sales for January were 3% above the prior year.

Synthetic scenario document for the Crocs hypothetical private-credit scenario. Inventory report for January 31, 2027, delivered February 18, 2027. Inventory at the lower of cost and net realizable value was $181.5 million. Inventory older than 180 days was 14.2% of inventory at cost, compared with 5.5% at origination, mostly winter product that arrived after its selling window. No write-down was recorded in January.

Synthetic scenario document for the Crocs hypothetical private-credit scenario. Updated 13-week cash forecast delivered February 22, 2027. Forecast Unrestricted Cash reaches a low of $41.3 million at the end of April 2027, against $35.0 million required and $52.0 million in the origination base forecast. The plan proposes deferring $4.0 million of new distribution capacity spending; it has not been approved.

event.presentation_summary: Reduced orders, older inventory and a lower cash forecast arrive together.
